Question 3(a) [4 marks]: Distinguish between transformed and transforming resources and provide an example of EACH in the context of the stimulus above.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
Wong Tong Noodle Bar Pty Ltd is a restaurant that has made a decision to cook their meals directly in front of the customer rather than behind kitchen doors. They believe that they might develop a competitive advantage over their competitors using this approach.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
1 each marks: For each correct definition
1 each marks: For each correct example


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Transformed resources are inputs changed or converted in the operations process: materials (cooking ingredients), information, customers (special orders or requests from the menu). Transforming resources are used to transform other resources but are not part of the finished product: human resources (cooks) and facilities (cooking utensils, kitchen equipment).

TEACHER MARKER COMMENTS:
Many students failed to provide an accurate distinction between transformed and transforming; terminology was weak. Most could give examples.
